Shared species and similarity corrected for unseen species

Source: R/shared.R
beta_shared.Rd

For every pair of sites:

  • beta_shared() estimates the total number of species the two sites share, including shared species that neither sample detected, with the Chao1-shared estimator for abundance data and the Chao2-shared estimator for incidence data (Chao et al. 2000; Pan et al. 2009).

  • beta_chao() gives the abundance-based Jaccard and Sørensen similarities of Chao et al. (2005), which correct for shared species missed by incomplete samples, next to the classic indices.

Classic indices underestimate similarity when samples are incomplete, because a species shared by two sites but rare in one of them is often missed. The Chao versions estimate the probability that an individual of one site belongs to a species shared with the other (u, v), adding the shared species that were seen once in one sample. They are the estimators of EstimateS and SpadeR; the values equal SpadeR's, and chao_jaccard equals one minus vegan's vegdist(method = "chao"). This is checked in the test suite.

Usage

beta_shared(
  data,
  site = site,
  species = species,
  abundance = NULL,
  unit = NULL,
  n_units = NULL,
  .by = NULL
)

beta_chao(
  data,
  site = site,
  species = species,
  abundance = NULL,
  unit = NULL,
  n_units = NULL,
  .by = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long format, with one row per record.

site, species

<tidy-select> The column holding site identifiers and the column holding species names.

abundance

<tidy-select> The column holding counts. If NULL (the default), a column called abundance is used when present, otherwise every row counts as one individual.

unit

For incidence data, the column naming the sampling unit (a trap, bait, plot or survey day) in which each species was detected. Each site is then described by the number of units in which each species was found and the number of units sampled, and every estimate is incidence-based (Chao et al. 2014), for TD, PD and FD alike. Leave NULL for abundance data.

n_units

For incidence data, a column giving the number of units sampled at each site, constant within a site. Use it when some units detected no species and so do not appear in the data. By default the number of distinct units in the data is used.

.by

<tidy-select> Optional grouping columns, kept in the output. Grouped data frames are also respected.

Value

beta_shared(): a tibble with the grouping columns, site_1, site_2, s_1, s_2 (observed richness), observed (observed shared species) and estimate. beta_chao(): a tibble with site_1, site_2, jaccard, sorensen (classic, on species lists), u, v, chao_jaccard and chao_sorensen (similarities, 0-1).

References

Chao, A., Hwang, W.-H., Chen, Y.-C. and Kuo, C.-Y. (2000). Estimating the number of shared species in two communities. Statistica Sinica, 10, 227-246.

Chao, A., Chazdon, R. L., Colwell, R. K. and Shen, T.-J. (2005). A new statistical approach for assessing similarity of species composition with incidence and abundance data. Ecology Letters, 8, 148-159. doi:10.1111/j.1461-0248.2004.00707.x

Pan, H.-Y., Chao, A. and Foissner, W. (2009). A nonparametric lower bound for the number of species shared by multiple communities. Journal of Agricultural, Biological and Environmental Statistics, 14, 452-468.
